Cc: contracts@pioneerhealth.com, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@pioneerhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Request: narrower SLO windowing & evidence package

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Pioneer is excited about the latency profile you showed in steady state. We ran a short production spike test last month and observed intermittent p95 spikes during a daily batch fan-in. Our procurement team asked whether we can: 1) codify a narrower measurement window for p50/p95 (so the contract tracks interactive traffic only), and 2) see the operational evidence Redwood would provide if we request a temporary carveout (what you would need from us + what you would share).

Specifically were asking:
- Can the SLO measurement be scoped to a configurable daypart (08:00–22:00 UTC) with aggregation that excludes scheduled batch ingestion windows?
- What evidence package does Redwood require to approve a temporary p95 relief? (logs, sampling artifacts, traffic profile, etc.)
- Is there a playbook for canary/fallback routing during the carveout?

Ive attached a short doc with the procurement team's requirements (pioneer_initial_ask.pdf). Can you share a proposed amendment or the evidence checklist? Wed like to get this into the contract negotiation next week.

Best,
Alex
Alex Reynolds
Head of Platform Partnerships, Pioneer Health

Subject: Re: Request: narrower SLO windowing & evidence package

Alex —

Appreciate the write-up and the attachment. Short answer: yes, we can support a daypart-limited measurement window and we have a defined evidence checklist for temporary relief requests. Ill summarize below and attach a draft amendment for internal review.

High level proposal (summary):
- Measurement window: 08:00–22:00 UTC for interactive SLOs (p50 and p95).
- Batch carveout mechanism: scheduled exclusions defined by mutually-agreed cron windows; exclusions must be declared 72 hours in advance for planned maintenance; emergency carveouts evaluated case-by-case with evidence.
- Evidence package: traffic profile (1/5/30m granularity), KW/endpoint map, sampling traces around spikes, server-side request IDs, and a 48–72 hour artifact bundle from your side. Redwood will supply internal sampling summaries, KV-cache hit rates, and a candidate canary routing plan.

Im copying Laura and Ben for legal/pricing language and to iterate the amendment. Ill pull together a short draft and our evidence checklist by Friday. Also linking our shared Drive space for the traffic-profile you mentioned: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/pioneer/traffic-profile-2026Q3

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Director, Account Strategy — Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Request: narrower SLO windowing & evidence package — proposed amendment language

Team — forwarding Pioneers ask and my proposed amendment language. Need quick alignment on three items before I send to Pioneer: pricing credit model during approved temporary relief, legal phrasing for scheduling and emergency carveouts, and operational acceptance criteria for canary routing.

Proposed amendment (sketch):
- "Daypart Measurement: Redwood and Customer agree that SLO measurements for interactive request latency (p50/p95) will be computed over the agreed daypart window 08:00–22:00 UTC. Any traffic outside this window will be excluded from SLO aggregation unless expressly designated by mutual written agreement."
- "Batch Exclusion: Customer may request scheduled Batch Exclusions by submitting a Batch Exclusion Notice at least 72 hours in advance. Emergency Exclusions require submission of an Evidence Package and are subject to Redwood review and approval. Redwood will provide a documented remediation plan and temporary routing adjustments as agreed."
- "Temporary Relief Credits: If a temporary relief is approved, Redwood may provide a proportional credit applied to the affected billing period; the credit model is a function of duration and measured impact. A pricing model will be provided during contract finalization."

Operational acceptance criteria (draft):
- Evidence package contents: traffic profile CSV, requestID-sampled traces (min 1% sampling), KV cache hit rates, sample latency distributions, and a short runbook of the batch job schedule.
- Canary plan items: split percentage, canary duration (min 2 hours), rollback thresholds, and monitoring dashboard links.

Ben: can you draft a succinct pricing clause we can offer (banded credit model) for an approved temporary relief?
Kimberly: want legal to confirm acceptable wording especially around "emergency" carveouts and "proportional credit". Laura: confirm operations SLA language mapping to the Console runbook.

Thanks — aiming to send to Pioneer early next week with the amendment draft attached.

—Rishi

Subject: Precision SLO windowing — amendment & evidence checklist (proposal)

Alex / Maria —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled internal alignment. Attached is our formal amendment draft and the Redwood Evidence Checklist (pioneer-slo-evidence.zip) that describes the artifacts well need to evaluate any emergency relief requests. The key points:

1) Measurement Window — we propose the interactive measurement window 08:00–22:00 UTC (will be codified in Section 2.1.a of the amendment).
2) Scheduled Batch Exclusions — must be declared 72 hours in advance using the Batch Exclusion Notice template (included).
3) Emergency Relief — requires the Evidence Checklist; Redwood will review within 24 hours and provide either an approval with remediation plan or a denial with rationale.
4) Temporary Relief Credits — proposed banded model (0.5% credit per 12-hour approved relief, capped at 10% / billing period). Ben has drafted the pricing clause and Kimberly has provided legal wording which Ive incorporated.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached amendment and evidence bundle.
- If acceptable, sign via DocuSign here: https://www.docusign.com/sign/XYZ-precision-amend (Ill also push this to your contracts inbox).
- If you prefer a working call, Im available next Tue/Wed to run through the canary plan and monitoring links.

Quoting your original ask for context:
> Can the SLO measurement be scoped to a configurable daypart (08:00–22:00 UTC) with aggregation that excludes scheduled batch ingestion windows?

Happy to iterate — the attached draft is intentionally prescriptive to avoid ambiguity.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Director, Account Strategy — Redwood Inference
